outline.description: Establishes the foundational facts of the case, the charges brought, the trial proceedings, and the procedural posture on appeal. This chapter provides the necessary context for understanding the legal issues that follow, including the applicable criminal statutes and standards of review.
subtopics: The November 2020 incident: domestic violence, kidnapping, and firearm possession
The felon in possession charge under 18 U.S.C. §§ 922(g)(1) and 924(e)
The Armed Career Criminal Act and enhanced penalties for violent felons
Trial proceedings and jury verdict
Sentencing outcome and calculation of the advisory guidelines range
Issues raised on appeal and applicable standards of review

outline.chapter_title: Rule 404(b) and the Intrinsic Evidence Doctrine
outline.description: Examines the central evidentiary dispute over whether testimony about Cutbank's prior possession of the sawed-off rifle constituted impermissible propensity evidence or admissible intrinsic evidence. This chapter explains the distinction between intrinsic evidence and Rule 404(b) evidence, and how prior possession of the same firearm can be used to prove ownership or control.
subtopics: Federal Rule of Evidence 404(b) and the prohibition on propensity evidence
The intrinsic evidence exception: evidence that is part of the charged offense
Prior possession of the same firearm as proof of ownership or control
The Battle precedent: United States v. Battle, 774 F.3d 504 (8th Cir. 2014)
Pretrial ruling on the admissibility of prior possession testimony
Trial testimony from D.F. and C.F. regarding prior observations of the firearm
Abuse of discretion standard for evidentiary rulings

outline.chapter_title: Confrontation Clause, Hearsay, and Cross-Examination Issues
outline.description: Addresses the procedural and constitutional challenges raised regarding trial testimony, including Confrontation Clause concerns about D.F.'s statements to police, requests for limiting instructions, and disputes over cross-examination and authentication of impeachment evidence. Concludes with an analysis of the harmless error and cumulative error doctrines.
subtopics: The request for a limiting instruction on D.F.'s statements to police
Confrontation Clause requirements when the hearsay declarant testifies at trial
The role of limiting instructions and the timing of jury instructions
Cross-examination impeachment and authentication requirements for police reports
The testimony about D.F.'s sister being killed by a gun and Rule 403 balancing
Harmless error analysis: whether errors substantially swayed the verdict
Cumulative error doctrine and substantial prejudice standard

outline.description: Analyzes the dispute over the four-level sentencing enhancement for possession of a firearm in connection with another felony offense. This chapter explains how the enhancement operates, the defendant's challenge based on 18 U.S.C. § 3553(a), and the appellate standards for reviewing both procedural and substantive reasonableness of within-range sentences.
subtopics: Presentence Investigation Report and the calculation of total offense level
USSG § 2K2.1(b)(6)(B): the four-level enhancement for possession in connection with another felony
Application of the enhancement without requiring a separate criminal charge or conviction
The defendant's argument that the enhancement conflicts with § 3553(a)'s parsimony principle
Procedural reasonableness: correct calculation of the Guidelines range under Gall v. United States
Substantive reasonableness and the presumption for within-range sentences
The district court's consideration of § 3553(a) factors and sentencing discretion
